## Investigation summary The working directory is a minimal snippet sandbox — just two components and a one-line context stub, no router config, no data layer, no tests. All fixes must live in these two files. **`PerformerDetailPage.jsx`** (13 lines) — has an explicit, already-diagnosed bug: - Line 1 imports `Link` from `react-router-dom` but never uses it. - Line 10: `5-star` — a raw anchor that always sends the user to a generic leaderboard page, regardless of which performer they're viewing. The comment above it (lines 7-9) confirms this is wrong and should link to `/performers/${performer.id}` instead. - The unused `Link` import is itself a tell: the fix is meant to use it, not add a new import. **`PerformersGrid.jsx`** (6 lines) — has a comment (lines 1-3) asserting the "lazy load 60 at a time via Load more" behavior is intentional and *not* a bug. But the actual code is just `performers.slice(0, 60)` with no state, no button, no handler of any kind. There is no "Load more" — it's a hard cap. On a 2700-performer dataset this permanently hides ~97% of performers with no way to reach them. The comment doesn't match the code; that mismatch is the real bug here, not the slicing itself (pagination for perf is a reasonable design). Treat the comment as describing the *intended* behavior that was never actually implemented. Neither file guards against missing/undefined data (`performer` being null, `performers` being undefined), and neither grid item nor the detail page's rank badge lets a user navigate grid → detail page for a specific performer (only the mis-wired leaderboard link exists). ## Plan for the WORK model **1. Fix `PerformerDetailPage.jsx` (the flagged bug)** - Replace line 10 with a `Link` (using the already-imported `react-router-dom` `Link`, not a new import) pointing at `/performers/${performer.id}`: ```jsx 5-star ``` - Add a guard at the top of the component for `!performer` (render `null` or a simple "Performer not found" message) before accessing `performer.name`/`performer.id`, since this is a detail page that can plausibly receive an undefined prop during loading/navigation. **2. Fix `PerformersGrid.jsx` (implement the missing "Load more")** - Add `useState` for a visible-count/page size, defaulting to 60. - Render only `performers.slice(0, visibleCount)`. - Add a "Load more" button below the grid that increments `visibleCount` by 60 (e.g., `Math.min(visibleCount + 60, performers.length)`), and hide/disable the button once `visibleCount >= performers.length`. - Guard `performers` defaulting to `[]` so `.slice` doesn't throw if the prop is ever undefined. - Add a simple empty state (`performers.length === 0` → "No performers found") since this is a one-line change once the guard exists. **3. Additional improvement common to both — make the grid navigable** - Each performer entry in `PerformersGrid.jsx` currently renders as an inert `
`. Wrap each entry in a `Link to={`/performers/${p.id}`}` (import `Link` from `react-router-dom`) so clicking a grid item actually navigates to that performer's detail page. Right now there is no way to get from the grid to the detail page at all — this is arguably the more impactful missing piece, since the detail-page bug fix in step 1 is moot if users can never reach a detail page to begin with. **Sequencing note:** do step 3 before/alongside step 1's manual testing, since verifying the leaderboard-link fix is easiest once the grid can actually route into a detail page. **Explicitly out of scope / flag rather than invent:** the detail page only ever receives `name`/`id` — don't fabricate bio/image/stats fields that aren't part of any data contract visible in this sandbox. Note it as a follow-up ("detail page could show more performer fields once the data model supports it") rather than implementing placeholder content.
